headline: Across tennis, movies and baseball (with chess as a skill-dominated control), the model's signature finding — the most successful are almost never the most skilled — does NOT corroborate: real top performers sit at the 99th+ percentile of independently measured skill (tennis #1 at 0.994), a configuration the faithful engine produces in ≤1.3% of its baseline runs.

metrics.label: Tennis #1-success skill percentile (titles)
metrics.note: decoupling ABSENT: Federer is at the top of measured skill; occurs in 1.3% of model runs. P2 band [0.55,0.95]/0.95 [PREVIEW-CALIBRATED; preview 0.994]

metrics.label: P(top-success in top-skill decile), tennis / movies
metrics.note: paper's printed 3% is its claim for the T>0.8 cut; the faithful engine gives ~27% at the true top-decile cut (C22). [PREVIEW-CALIBRATED <25% band]

metrics.label: Elite persistence ladder (y2y Spearman)
metrics.note: pre-declared measured ladder reproduced exactly; but decoupling does NOT order with it -> partial ordering

metrics.label: Success top-20% share (fat tail / P1)
metrics.note: shape present everywhere but consistent with ANY multiplicative mechanism. *tennis threshold-sensitive (0.639 vs 0.6 [PREVIEW-CALIBRATED])

metrics.label: Poker Main-Event repeat-champion test (1990-2025)
metrics.note: modern fields ~8-10k -> cannot distinguish skill from luck; poker leg rests on Levitt-Miles 2014 literature

tables.title: P2 decoupling verdicts (independent ex-ante skill proxies)

figures.caption: Skill percentile of the top-success unit (orange, 95% CI) and top-10 median (blue) per domain, against the TvL baseline winner percentile (0.70) and its model band [0.55,0.95]. Every measured domain sits in the model's talent-dominated corner (>=0.95) — decoupling absent.
figures.alt: Error-bar plot: tennis, movies, baseball winner skill percentiles near 1.0, far above the dashed TvL baseline at 0.70.

figures.caption: Elite persistence (x) vs top-success decoupling (y). The pre-declared persistence ladder chess>tennis>baseball holds, but decoupling stays ~1.0 regardless of luck share — opposite the TvL p_L={20,50,80} ladder (blue), which moves winner percentile only within 0.67-0.73.
figures.alt: Scatter: tennis and baseball at winner-pct ~1.0 and lower persistence; TvL p_L ladder clustered near 0.7 at high persistence.

figures.caption: Success is fat-tailed in every domain (top-20% share far above the egalitarian 0.20 line) from near-symmetric skill — the P1 shape signature, consistent with any multiplicative mechanism.
figures.alt: Three bar panels (tennis, movies, science) showing success top-20% shares of 0.64-0.93 versus a 0.20 reference and the TvL capital share 0.77.

notes: Signature finding (most successful != most skilled) does NOT corroborate in tennis/movies/baseball; shape finding (fat tail) does, but is not evidence for the model's mechanism.
C22: the paper's released engine gives P(winner talent>0.8)=7.8%, not the printed 3% — printed values treated as the paper's claims throughout.

Prior art: not the first talent-vs-luck/sports test; closest = Janosov-Battiston-Sinatra 2020, Zappala et al. 2023 (a~0.20-0.30). Biondo-Pluchino SSRN 6572147 (2026) is concurrent and NOT yet read (metadata-verified; bot-blocked) — a human should read it before external publication.
Thresholds set with Phase-2a previews in view are labelled [PREVIEW-CALIBRATED]; 'pre-registered'/'validated' are not used for them. Tennis P1 (0.639 vs 0.6) is threshold-sensitive.
Deviations: unstaged tvl-engine/qa-distcheck/recency files substituted by the faithful replication engine + spec-quoted constants; funding verdict and model-fit deferred to study 002.
